chances.title: About 44 in 100 got in. Where you live changed the odds.

lede.s: 102,988 students applied for fall 2025. 45,674 got in. Californians got in at about 37 in 100. Out-of-state students got in at about 63 in 100. Those are different pools, so it's not a shortcut. The rest of this page is what you control.
lede.p: 102,988 students applied for fall 2025. 45,674 got in. Californians got in at about 37 in 100. Out-of-state students got in at about 63 in 100. Those are different pools, so it's not a shortcut. The rest of this page is what your student controls.

chances.src: Fall 2025 first-years (C1): California 25,473 of 68,593 admitted (37.1%). Out of state 8,315 of 13,149 (63.2%). International 11,886 of 21,246 (55.9%). Overall 45,674 of 102,988 (44.3%).

ladder.kicker: What UC Davis actually cares about
ladder.title: Only 2 things are top-tier: your classes and your GPA.
ladder.lede: By senior fall, those are mostly set. Your essays, which UC calls Personal Insight Questions (PIQs), sit one step down with activities and volunteering. They're the biggest piece you can still change before Nov 30.
considered: First in your family to go to college
not_considered: How often you toured or emailed
ladder.note: Second tier = where your hours go before Nov 30 ↓
ladder.src: Section C7, first-year admission factors, 2025–26 Common Data Set.

numbers.lede: Type your UC GPA (the weighted one UC calculates) to see where it sits next to UC Davis's first-years. This is a range, not a cutoff.

gpa.near: Right around UC Davis's average. Your classes and GPA are the top tier, so you're in the conversation. Now your PIQs and activities make the case.
gpa.above: Above UC Davis's average. Good start. Your PIQs and activities are the next tier, so make them count.
gpa.below: Below UC Davis's average. That's not a no. Your PIQs and activities are the next tier down, and they're what you can still change. Put your hours there.

facts.text: of enrolled first-years reported a GPA of 4.0 or higher.

numbers.src: Sections C11–C12: enrolled first-years, fall 2025 (100% reported a GPA). The CDS reports an average above 4.0, so it's a weighted GPA. UC Davis doesn't use SAT/ACT scores in admission (C7, C8).

money.title: If you qualify for aid, UC Davis meets about 82% of need on average.
money.lede: The sticker price isn't your price. The net price calculator gives your family a real estimate in about 15 minutes.
money.aid_line: Just over half of first-years get need-based grants. First-years who got aid averaged $32,557 a year.
money.npc_label: Find UC Davis's net price calculator →
money.src: Sections G1 (2026–27 first-year tuition and required fees) and H2 (81.7% of need met; line J average package of first-years awarded aid), 2025–26 Common Data Set. On-campus food and housing (about $22,125) cost extra.

todo.title: 4 moves, aimed at what UC Davis rates highest.

items.title: Check your courses against your transcript.
items.body: The UC application has you type in every class and grade yourself. Match it line by line. Your classes and GPA are UC Davis's whole top tier, so one typo matters.

items.title: Read your 4 PIQs in one sitting.
items.body: PIQs are the next tier here, right next to activities. If two tell the same story, swap one for a side of you the reader hasn't met yet.

items.title: Put a number on every activity.
items.body: Hours a week, people you led, what changed because of you. Activities and volunteering sit right next to your PIQs at UC Davis.

items.title: Engineering? Pick the exact major.
items.body: UC Davis's College of Engineering has no undeclared option. You apply to one specific engineering major, so choose it on purpose.

todo.done: All 4 done. That's a real application. ✓

title.s: Are your PIQs doing their job?
title.p: Are your student's PIQs doing their job?

lede.s: PIQs are one step below the top tier at UC Davis, and they're the biggest piece you can still change. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read all 4 of your PIQs together, then tap what's true.
lede.p: PIQs are one step below the top tier at UC Davis, and they're the biggest piece your student can still change. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read all 4 of your student's PIQs together, then tap what's true.

items.title: Each one answers the exact question asked.
items.body: Circle the key words in the question. Every paragraph should answer them, not a question close to them.

items.title: Only you could have written it.
items.body: Swap in a friend's name. If it still works, it isn't specific enough yet.

items.title: It shows what you did.
items.body: Your role, your steps, what changed. Not just what the team or club did.

items.title: The 4 show 4 different sides of you.
items.body: If two PIQs tell the same story, swap one for a side of you the reader hasn't met yet.

after.s: Not sure you can check all four? That's normal. It's hard to judge your own writing.
after.p: Not sure? That's normal. It's hard to judge writing you're close to.

self_check.all_done: All 4. Nice work. A fresh reader can still catch what you can't see.

take.heading: What I saw as an admissions reader
take.quote: At UC Davis, the top tier is your transcript, and by now it's mostly written. So your PIQs carry the rest. Use them to explain what your grades can't: what you did, why it mattered and what changed because of you.
